questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook healthy meals quickly
The history of popcorn and crisps
Why snacks are unhealthy for children
Why snacking has become so popular around the world
questions.why: They find out why people around the world are so in love with snack food.

questions.q: According to Beth, how much is spent on snacks around the world each year?
options: About $1.5 billion
About $1.5 trillion
Just over $15 trillion
About $150 million
questions.why: Beth says an estimated $1.5 trillion a year is spent globally on snacking.

questions.q: What is food historian Annie Gray's favourite snack?
options: Salted peanuts and a banana, eaten together
A small round cheese bread made with cassava
A chocolate sandwich
A bag of crisps
questions.why: She likes salted peanuts and bananas, 'preferably together'.

questions.q: What is 'chipa', chef Barbara Oievari's favourite snack?
options: A sweet cake made with bananas
A type of salty crisp
A small round bun made with cassava and cheese
A cheese sandwich that is popular in Florida and Argentina
questions.why: She describes it as a small, round bun made with cassava, cheese, butter, milk and salt.

questions.q: What do Neil and Beth say about their own favourite snack?
options: Both love crisps, though Neil wishes he could say something healthy
Neil prefers fresh fruit, but Beth prefers crisps and chocolate bars
They both prefer chocolate to anything salty
Neither of them eats snacks between meals
questions.why: Neil wants to say something healthy but loves crisps, and Beth says 'me too'.

questions.q: According to Christine Cochran, why do snacks stay popular when money is tight?
options: They are healthier and more filling than a full sit-down meal
Shops give them away for free
They last longer than fresh food
They are a small treat that people can afford
questions.why: She calls a snack 'an affordable luxury' you can turn to when money is tight.

questions.q: What else does Christine Cochran say consumers want?
options: Bigger packets to share with family
Snacks made only from traditional recipes that their grandparents used
Small, easy portions with ingredients for things like gut health
Snacks that replace breakfast
questions.why: She says people want smaller, convenient portions and specific functional ingredients like gut health.

questions.q: Why does Barbara say it is ironic that her son likes baked cheddar snacks?
options: Because he usually refuses to eat cheese
Because they are similar to her own favourite, just more modern
Because they are much more expensive than the chipa she makes at home
Because she makes them for him at home
questions.why: She says they are baked with cheese, 'similar to what I enjoy – it's just the modern twist'.
